correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the lower central series by u-degree. One may use u=r−r⁻¹ itself, which has leading term 2(r−1) and is negated by s. Its ideal is nilpotent with semisimple quotient k×k, hence is J. For a,c≥1 and b,d∈{0,1}, the bracket is ((−1)^(bc)−(−1)^(ad))u^(a+c)s^(b+d). In any even target degree t the only possible image is k u^t s, and in odd target degree t both basis vectors are allowed. Bracketing degree t−1 with degree one generates the full allowed target: for even t use the two different parity-of-s basis vectors in the odd degrees; for odd t use u^(t−1)s against u and us. This works also with the restricted degree-(t−1) image from the previous lower central term. Thus for i≥2 the i-th Lie term is exactly the sum of the allowed spaces in degrees t≥i through p−1. Nilpotence J^p=0 makes the associative exp/log and BCH identities valid in degrees

value.rationale: The lower central quotients are natural structural invariants of the distinguished modular unit group. The alternating dimensions describe every noncentral commutator layer uniformly over primes and extension fields; a center computation or class bound cannot substitute for that profile. The exact series resolves sharpness and supplies the number of generators without separately assuming either invariant.
residual_risks: No extension to rotations of order p^a for a>1 or to characteristic two is credited.
